pairs.statement: The commercial sections keep the cases filed before them before the new courts are installed.
A court claim interrupts limitation even if filed before a court that has no jurisdiction.
The petition must name the court before which the claim is brought, on pain of formal inadmissibility.
The family section hears claims on guardianship and its loss, interdiction, absence, disappearance and the appointment of a curator.
The president of the family section has the powers of the urgent-matters judge.
A section president at the specialised commercial court may take provisional or protective measures in summary proceedings.
The action goes to the real-estate section, subject to the special rules on publishing actions to rescind, annul, modify or set aside rights based on published deeds.
The court decides every case within its territory, notably civil, commercial, maritime, social, real-property and family cases.
The social section alone hears disputes on staff-delegate elections, union rights, strikes, social security and retirement, and collective agreements.
The territorial rules of the procedure code, the commercial and maritime codes and special texts apply to the commercial section.
The family section hears claims to prove a marriage or filiation and claims on kafala.
The new jurisdiction rules for the specialised commercial courts apply from the date those courts are installed.
In real-property matters and in actions on leases of immovables, commercial leases included, the action goes only to the court where the property is.
In family matters: divorce and return to the marital home go to the court of the marital home, custody and visitation to where custody is exercised, maintenance to the creditor's domicile.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The statement includes divorce without distinguishing the expressly different venue for divorce by mutual consent: «وفي الطلاق بالتراضي بمكان إقامة أحد الزوجين حسب اختيارهما».

pairs.statement: The social section alone hears the proof, performance, suspension and termination of employment, training and apprenticeship contracts.
Hearings are public unless publicity would harm public order, morals or the privacy of the family.
The court in social matters sits as a judge with worker and employer assessors; absent assessors are replaced by substitutes or by judges.
The family section hears maintenance, custody and visitation claims.
When specialised commercial subject is yes, the case leaves the ordinary courts (specialisedCommercialCourt).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The rules apply «ابتداء من تاريخ تنصيب الجهات القضائية الجديدة», and earlier cases remain with the existing bodies: «وتبقى الجهات القضائية الإدارية والأقسام التجارية مختصة بالفصل في الدعاوى المرفوعة أمامها قبل تاريخ تنصيب الجهات القضائية الجديدة».

pairs.statement: Cases are listed before the sections according to the nature of the dispute.
The civil section of the court hears this claim.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text does not identify this claim's nature or establish that it belongs to the civil section. The express residual rule applies where sections have not been created and excludes social cases.

pairs.statement: When public body party is yes, the case leaves the ordinary courts (administrativeCourt).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The rule has express exceptions: «باستثناء المنازعات الموكلة إلى جهات قضائية أخرى». Article 802 states «يكون من اختصاص المحاكم العادية المنازعات الآتية», including «مخالفات الطرق» and the specified public-vehicle damage claims.

pairs.statement: By way of exception to the administrative courts, the ordinary courts hear road offences and liability claims for damage caused by a vehicle of the State, a wilaya, a commune or a public administrative body.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The ordinary courts' jurisdiction is stated, but the excerpt does not identify articles 800 and 801 as administrative-court jurisdiction rules.

pairs.statement: The real-estate section hears disputes about real property.
The president of the social section may order urgent provisional or protective measures to stop anything that obstructs the freedom to work.
Territorial jurisdiction in real-property matters lies with the court where the property is, unless the law says otherwise.
The paragraphs on the specialised poles were repealed from the CPCA article on the court's make-up.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text repeals paragraphs 7–10 of article 32, but does not say that those paragraphs concern specialised poles or identify article 32 as concerning the court's make-up.

pairs.statement: The court may also be made up of specialised poles.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The possibility of forming specialised poles is stated, but this excerpt does not identify the subject of «تتشكل» as the court.

pairs.statement: The court is the court of general jurisdiction and is made up of sections.
Additional requests that follow from the main request are admitted before the social section at every stage, even if they were not put to conciliation.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The rule for additional requests is stated, but the excerpt does not say that it applies before the social section.

pairs.statement: In courts where the sections have not been created, the civil section hears every dispute except social cases.

The real-estate section hears in particular ownership and real rights, possession and prescription, property development, co-ownership, proof of ownership, pre-emption, gifts and bequests of real property, and transfers of ownership.
The public prosecutor is a principal party in every case applying the Family Code.
Urgent matters and requests for protective measures are brought by petition before the court where the problem or measure arises.
pairs.missingOrWrong: For protective measures, the text specifies «غير منظم بإجراءات خاصة». It does not establish the same petition and venue rule for protective measures governed by special procedures.

pairs.statement: When (the petition asks for wages or the petition asks for reinstatement) and court has section for matter is no, the case leaves the ordinary courts (otherSection).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text does not identify wage or reinstatement claims, equate absence of the relevant section with absence of sections generally, or say that such cases leave the ordinary courts for 'otherSection'.

pairs.statement: The courts sitting in social matters hear individual labour disputes arising from the performance, suspension or ending of an employment relationship.
Where the contract ended or was suspended because of a work accident or an occupational illness, the court of the plaintiff's domicile has jurisdiction.
In a social dispute the territorial court is that of the place where the employment contract was made or performed, or of the defendant's domicile.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The territorial connecting factors are stated, but the excerpt does not establish that this rule governs social disputes generally.

pairs.statement: The commercial section hears commercial disputes, except those given to the specialised commercial court.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The excerpt excludes disputes mentioned in article 536 مكرر, but does not say that those disputes are assigned to the specialised commercial court.

pairs.statement: Lack of subject-matter jurisdiction is a matter of public order that the court raises of its own motion at any stage.

The specialised commercial court hears disputes on intellectual property, commercial companies, judicial settlement and bankruptcy, banks and financial institutions with merchants, maritime and air transport, insurance linked to commercial activity, and international trade.
The real-estate section hears agricultural leases.
The president of the real-estate section may order urgent protective measures even when there is a serious dispute.
In its former wording, the article gave the commercial section commercial disputes and, where relevant, maritime disputes.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The jurisdiction described is stated, but the excerpt does not say that this is the article's former wording.

pairs.statement: The territorial rules of the procedure code apply to the specialised commercial court.
A case listed before the wrong section is sent to the right section through the registry, after the court president has been told.

The administrative courts are the general courts of administrative disputes and hear cases in which the State, a wilaya, a commune, a public administrative body, a national public institution or a national professional organisation is a party.
The family section hears claims on engagement, marriage, return to the marital home, and the dissolution of marriage and its consequences.
The real-estate section hears claims to annul, rescind, amend or undo rights arising from published deeds.
The real-estate section hears leases of dwellings and of professional premises.
The president of the commercial section may take urgent provisional or protective measures.
The social section sits, on pain of nullity, as a presiding judge with assessors under labour legislation.
The real-estate section hears partition and boundary-marking.
The real-estate section hears disputes between farmers, or with third parties, on agricultural land of the national domain.
